canonical_statement: For every commutative Dedekind domain R, the monoid of integral ideals of R is a unique factorization monoid, and every nonzero integral ideal I is the finite product of its height-one prime-power components. The unit ideal is included as the empty-product boundary case; the zero ideal is excluded.
domain_and_universes: universe u; R : Type u; CommRing R; IsDedekindDomain R; I : Ideal R; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: I != 0 for the explicit finite-product conjunct
conclusion: UniqueFactorizationMonoid (Ideal R), together with finprod v, v.maxPowDividing I = I for every nonzero I.
